factual_claims.claim: On August 2, 2026, the European Commission's AI Office and national competent authorities began enforcing key provisions of the Artificial Intelligence Act, marking the start of mandatory transparency obligations and general-purpose AI rules.

Under the new EU AI Act rules enforced in August 2026, interactive systems such as chatbots must explicitly inform users when they are interacting with AI, deepfakes must be clearly labeled, and AI-generated content must carry machine-readable marks.
General-Purpose AI model providers are required under the EU AI Act to document technical information, implement copyright policies, and publish detailed summaries of their training content.
Rules regarding high-risk AI systems under the EU AI Act have been postponed to late 2027 and 2028 under the AI Omnibus.
